title: Open and Closed Hi-Hat
description: Hear the difference between a tight hi-hat and a loose one, and try each with the kick and snare.

steps.title: One cymbal, two sounds
steps.description: A hi-hat is two cymbals stacked on a stand, with a foot pedal underneath. With the pedal down, the cymbals are clamped shut and you get a short "tick". Lift your foot and they're loose, so a hit rings out as a long "tsss". Most of the time drummers keep it closed. An open hit here and there gives the beat a little lift.

steps.title: Closed hat
steps.description: Hit the closed hi-hat. Short and tight. This is the sound you'll hear ticking away in most beats.
steps.hint: The green pad labelled CHH, third along the top row.

steps.title: Open hat
steps.description: Now the open hi-hat. Listen to how long it hangs on compared to the closed one.
steps.hint: It's right next to the closed hat, at the end of the top row. Look for OHH.

steps.title: Kick and closed hat
steps.description: Hit the kick and closed hi-hat together. That's the sound of beat 1 in a basic groove.
steps.hint: Get both pads close together in time. It doesn't need to be perfect.

steps.title: Snare and closed hat
steps.description: Now the snare with the closed hi-hat. In rock, that's beats 2 and 4.
steps.hint: SNR and CHH are both on the top row, with one pad between them.

steps.title: Kick and open hat
steps.description: Try the kick with the open hi-hat. It sounds bigger and pushier. Drummers often open the hat just before a snare hit to lean into it.
steps.hint: KCK and OHH sit at opposite ends of the top row.

steps.title: Tell them apart
steps.description: So what actually changes when you go from a closed hi-hat to an open one?

quizOptions.label: Closed is short and tight, open rings out
Open is played with a stick, closed with the foot
